scripts.title: Teleprompter and microphone test
scripts.notes: A 30-second test so the studio can check your sound before the first real recording. Read it at your normal pace.

segments.title: Setup test
segments.say: Hi, I'm Joshua Newsome, a Board Certified Behavior Analyst with Newsome Behavioral Health. This is a short test of the teleprompter and the microphone. I'm reading at my normal pace, in the room where I'll record. One, two, three, four, five. Thank you for watching, and I'll see you in the next video.

scripts.title: First-Then, Step by Step: your opening and closing
scripts.notes: Approved. Record each line 2-3 times, with a few seconds of silence before and after. Say only these words (tell the studio if you want to change any). Save as parents-02_owner-voice and put it in the inbox folder.

segments.title: Opening (about 17 s)
segments.say: "First shoes, then the park." It sounds simple, and it's easy to get wrong. I'm Joshua Newsome, a Board Certified Behavior Analyst. I wrote this video to show you five steps that make first-then work. From here, an AI-generated voice reads my script.

segments.title: Closing (about 22 s)
segments.say: Thanks for watching. Here's my one ask for this week: pick one routine, just one, and try first-then with a "then" your child loves. If it doesn't click right away, that's not failure. It's information. Every child is different. Start small, keep your promises, and be patient, with your child and with yourself. Until next time.

scripts.title: How to Become an RBT: your opening and closing
scripts.notes: Approved (series launches Tue Dec 1, 2026). Use the same room and microphone for every episode of this series. Save as rbt-01_owner-voice and put it in the inbox folder.

segments.title: Opening (about 22 s)
segments.say: Hi, I'm Joshua Newsome. I'm a Board Certified Behavior Analyst and the owner of Newsome Behavioral Health. This is episode one of a free series that covers everything on the RBT exam outline, and what each task looks like on a real shift. From here, you'll hear an AI narration voice reading a script I've reviewed. I'll see you at the end.

segments.title: Closing (about 22 s)
segments.say: That's the roadmap. Each week, we'll take one piece of the exam outline and show you what it looks like on a real shift, with practice questions you can try. If this helped, subscribe so you don't miss the next one. And tell me in the comments: which step are you on right now? You've got this.

scripts.title: What an RBT Does: your opening and closing
scripts.notes: Approved. Same room and microphone as your other RBT episodes. Record each line 2-3 times, with a few seconds of silence before and after. Say only these words.

segments.title: Opening (about 19 s)
segments.say: A parent stops you at pickup: "Can we stop the token board? He seems bored with it." What do you say? I'm Joshua Newsome, a Board Certified Behavior Analyst. This video gives you the answer, and the rules behind it. From here, an AI-generated voice reads my script.

segments.title: Closing (about 26 s)
segments.say: Thanks for watching. Here's one thing to do this week: ask your supervisor how you'll meet your supervision each month, and where your records are kept. Good supervisors welcome that question. And if the job feels heavy some days, say so early. Asking for support is part of being a professional. This job matters, and you don't have to figure it out alone. Until next time.

segments.title: Opening (about 17 s)
segments.say: Hi, I'm Joshua Newsome, a Board Certified Behavior Analyst and owner of Newsome Behavioral Health. This is episode three of Behavior Tech Foundations: the core vocabulary every other episode, and the exam, builds on. From here, an AI-generated voice reads my script.

segments.title: Closing (about 22 s)
segments.say: That's the foundation. Every procedure in this series, from prompting to differential reinforcement, is built from these pieces, so make them automatic. Here's my one ask: try the three practice questions again tomorrow, without looking. If this helped, subscribe, and tell me in the comments which term still feels fuzzy. Keep going. Until next time.

scripts.title: Operational Definitions: your opening and closing
scripts.notes: Approved. Same room and microphone as your other RBT episodes. Record each line 2-3 times, with a few seconds of silence before and after. Say only these words.

segments.title: Opening (about 18 s)
segments.say: I'm Joshua Newsome, a Board Certified Behavior Analyst and the owner of Newsome Behavioral Health. Every number on a data sheet starts with a definition. Get the definition right, and your data can mean something. From here, an AI-generated voice reads my script.

segments.title: Closing (about 23 s)
segments.say: That's operational definitions. Here's a challenge for this week: pick one everyday behavior, your own or your dog's, and write a definition a stranger could use. Then count it with a friend and see if you match. It's the same skill you'll use on every shift. Thanks for studying with us. Until next time.
